I'm an economist at U.S. Bank, where I lead the design of the economic scenarios behind the bank's stress tests and loan-loss reserves. Before that, I spent four years as an international economist at the U.S. Treasury.

[Email](mailto:nicholas.baulch@gmail.com) · [GitHub](https://github.com/nbaulch) · [Resume](resume.qmd)

## About

At U.S. Bank, I lead the team that designs the economic scenarios used for stress testing (CCAR) and loan-loss reserving (CECL), and I brief senior leadership each month on macroeconomic risks. I rebuilt the team's scenario production system as an R package, and I lead AI adoption for the bank's corporate finance division.

At Treasury, I was the lead economist on Ukraine after Russia's 2022 invasion, and I coordinated Treasury's support for the Federal Reserve's emergency lending facilities during COVID-19. I also worked on IMF lending and sovereign debt. I came to government as a Presidential Management Fellow at the IRS, after starting my career in analytics at Cardinal Health. I have an M.A. in international economics and finance from Johns Hopkins SAIS.

## Charts

I keep a small set of charts on the U.S. economy current, built from public data. Several maintain analyses first published by other economists, with credit to the original authors.

- [The AI economy](ai-economy.qmd): AI investment, adoption, and productivity.
- [Interest rates](interest-rates.qmd): the 10-year Treasury yield and the supply of long-term debt.
- [Inflation](inflation.qmd): measures of consumer price inflation.
